evidence_quotes: A historic building’s character can contribute to its commercial appeal as a hotel. Realising that opportunity takes architectural know-how to preserve original features while accommodating modern services and daily operations.

The conversion of a 19th-century mansion in Marseille brought these demands into focus. Originally built in 1860 and enriched with neo-Renaissance details, the building had served as offices for much of its later life before becoming a 51-room hospitality venue.
data.reason: The article is an educational piece providing professional advice and commentary on the architectural challenges of converting historic buildings into hotels, rather than reporting on a specific development or event of the company.
